memories.text: I'm still in Hamburg for now, renting near the harbour, and the rent keeps creeping up every year.
I plan freight routes at Nordlicht Logistics and most days it's spreadsheets and angry phone calls.
If anyone asks, I'm a logistics planner: I figure out which truck goes where and in what order.
Earl Grey is my tea, and I take it strong with a slice of lemon.
Give me the answer first and the reasoning after, otherwise I lose patience halfway through.
People assume cats set me off because I sneeze a lot, but I'm not allergic to cats at all.
My sister Freya lives in Aarhus and is expecting her first baby in the spring.
Our weekly planning call is on Monday mornings at nine, before anyone has had coffee.
Weekly route planning goes like this: pull the shipment backlog, cluster by postcode, check driver hours, and lock the plan by Thursday noon.
They've put me on Polaris, a project to digitise all our port paperwork.
Polaris just had its kickoff, and right now it's all workshops and wish lists.
I joined the Elbe Chess Club, and we meet on Wednesday evenings in a pub basement.
We spent Easter in the Lofoten Islands, and the fishing villages were unreal even in the sleet.
I'm lactose intolerant, so dairy is off the menu unless I remember the pills.
When I wax my skis I scrape the old wax, iron on the base layer, let it cool for thirty minutes, and brush from tip to tail.
Small correction: the weekly planning call is on Tuesdays now, Mondays were too chaotic.
My parents' anniversary dinner is booked at Rive Gauche for next month.
Scratch that, Rive Gauche cancelled on us, so the anniversary dinner moved to a place called Smak.
Polaris is owned by the Arctic Freight Group, which is why budget approvals take forever.
Polaris is delayed again because the customs software vendor keeps missing deadlines.
Went to the Elbphilharmonie for a jazz night and the acoustics are as good as everyone says.
Our cat has started knocking every plant off the windowsill at five in the morning.
I don't drive at all, I never got my licence and the trains here are great anyway.
Remind me to renew my German passport before the end of October.
We moved to Oslo in April, and I can see the fjord if I lean out of the bathroom window.
I started at Fjordline Energy in April as a planning lead, which is a big step up for me.
Fjordline Energy has its headquarters in Stavanger, so I'll be on the coastal train now and then.
My manager at the new place is Ingrid Solberg, who used to run offshore logistics.
Ingrid lives in Bergen and comes over to Oslo every other week.
I signed up for the B2 Norwegian exam in December, so my evenings are vocabulary flashcards now.
I've drifted from my old tea to sencha green tea, which is gentler on my stomach.
Polaris is finally live in three ports, and the customs team actually sent us a cake.
Just back from a week of skiing in Trysil, and my legs are completely destroyed.
I passed the B2 Norwegian exam, so I can finally argue with my landlord properly.
For gravlax I cure the salmon with salt, sugar, and dill for 48 hours, flipping it every 12.
I've never been to the United States, which surprises people given my line of work.
I've been collecting jazz piano records, mostly old pressings from flea markets.
Remind me to file the Norwegian tax return before the end of April.
